description.short_caption: Fungal colony growth on a blood agar plate.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a blood agar plate with a large, irregularly shaped fungal colony. The colony appears white to grayish in color with a fluffy texture, suggesting a filamentous fungus. The surrounding agar is red, consistent with blood agar medium. No additional colonies or bacterial growth are visible.

description.short_caption: Fungal colony growth on an agar plate.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a culture plate with a fungal colony exhibiting a white, fluffy, and cottony texture. The colony appears to have a central dense area with peripheral spreading. The agar medium is translucent, and the fungal growth is prominent against the background. The plate is photographed from above, and the texture and morphology of the colony suggest a filamentous fungus.
visible_findings: central dense area with peripheral spreading

description.short_caption: AFB broth culture showing growth of organisms.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a liquid broth culture tube, likely used for acid-fast bacilli (AFB) detection. The tube contains a pinkish liquid medium with visible white clumps or colonies settled at the bottom, indicative of microbial growth. The tube is labeled with barcodes and other identifiers, and the setup appears to be in a laboratory environment. The growth pattern is consistent with organisms such as Mycobacterium species.
visible_findings: white clumps or colonies at the bottom
